description: One of the largest airlines in the world, American Airlines transports both passengers and cargo through major cities including Los Angeles, Madrid, and Tokyo. Tracing its origins back to 1926, the company formerly known as AMR Corp. assumed its present-day name in 2013 after announcing its merger with US Airways Group.

title: American Airlines Group

rankings.title: Fortune 500
rankings.itemDescription:
The Fort Worth–based airline, one of the world’s largest carriers by passenger capacity, saw demand recover in 2022, following the COVID-19 pandemic slump. The company rose 25 spots in the Fortune 500.

  • Its revenue rose 64% to $49 billion in 2022, and the number of miles traveled by paying passengers rose 34%.

  • The airline group cut over 1,000 flights in July and August of 2022 in an effort to curb disruptions and account for soaring costs and labor shortages.

  • In early 2022, American Airlines partnered with Microsoft to set up access to cloud services and streamline ground operations.

  • Just like its airline peers, American has an upbeat forecast for 2023 even as pilot and aircraft shortages hold back its capacity. The company plans to hire 2,000 new pilots in 2023 for its mainline operations, but has yet to agree on a new labor contract with its pilots.

rankings.title: Fortune 500
rankings.itemDescription: Formed in 2013 by the merger of American Airlines and U.S. Airways, the company provides air transportation to 350 destinations in 50 countries. The largest carrier on the 500 list was hit hard by the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020. It lost $8.9 billion as its sales nosedived 62%, causing it to drop from No. 70 to No. 174 in the rankings this year. The new year didn't start much better as revenue declined 50% year-over-year in the first quarter of 2021 with a significant decrease in passenger flight sales but an increase in cargo flight revenue.

rankings.title: Fortune Global 500
rankings.itemDescription: American Airlines ceded its title as the leading airline in the U.S. to Delta, in an uneven year marked by labor disputes and the grounding of the Boeing 737 MAX planes. The latter caused the airline to cancel 10,000 flights in the fourth quarter alone. While the carrier's profits did rise 19%, to $1.7 billion, on $45.8 billion in revenues (up 2.8%), its hopes for a stronger showing in 2020 have since been scuttled by the coronavirus. After losing $2.2 billion in the first quarter alone and accepting government aid, American is shrinking its passenger fleet, the world’s largest. “Never before has our airline, or our industry, faced such a significant challenge,” CEO Doug Parker said in April.
